goal: For every natural number n there exists a prime p with n <= p
note: Mathlib states this with <=. Verified present via Loogle. Direct citation should close it.

goal: For every natural number n there exists a prime p with n < p
note: Mathlib gives n <= p. Needs exists_infinite_primes (n+1) plus arithmetic, so citation alone is not enough.

goal: A finite group whose order is prime is cyclic
note: Verified present via Loogle. Needs Fact (Nat.Prime p) instance handling.
Floor. A model failing this cannot write Lean at all.

goal: For every natural number n, n + 0 = n
note: Floor, with a bound variable.

goal: 7 is a prime number
note: Tests whether the model reaches for norm_num rather than a manual argument.

goal: For every real number x, x squared is non-negative
note: Also decidable by SymPy, so it doubles as a routing check.

goal: Every subgroup of a cyclic group is cyclic
note: Mathlib has Subgroup.isCyclic; the work is stating it correctly.

goal: A continuous real-valued function on a compact set attains its maximum
note: Extreme value theorem. In Mathlib, but the statement needs topology instances.

goal: The real numbers are uncountable
note: In Mathlib as a cardinality result; formalising it faithfully is the hard part.

goal: Every vector space has a basis
note: Requires the axiom of choice. In Mathlib, but heavily typeclass-laden.

goal: The continuous image of a compact set is compact
note: Standard result; tests whether retrieval finds topology lemmas at all.

goal: The square root of 2 is irrational
note: Nat.Prime.irrational_sqrt exists; connecting it to the statement is the work.

goal: Every even integer greater than 2 and less than 100 is the sum of two primes
note: Bounded, so decidable in principle, but no lemma exists. Tests decomposition.

goal: If a prime p satisfies p mod 4 = 1 then p is a sum of two squares
note: Fermat's theorem on sums of two squares. Hard even with Mathlib.

goal: For non-negative reals a and b, the square root of (a times b) is at most (a+b)/2
note: No one-shot lemma verified via Loogle. Mathlib has the squared form two_mul_le_add_sq, not the square-root form; nlinarith only closes it given the hint sq_nonneg (sqrt a - sqrt b), which appears nowhere in the goal.

goal: For every natural number n greater than 1, n^4 + 4 is not prime
note: No lemma about n^4+4 exists in Mathlib. The proof turns on the factorisation n^4+4 = (n^2-2n+2)(n^2+2n+2), which retrieval cannot surface; natural-number subtraction makes the factors treacherous to state directly.

goal: The sum of the first n odd numbers equals n squared
note: Mathlib has Gauss's Finset.sum_range_id, not this sum. Provable by induction or by routing through sum_range_id, but either way the agent must construct the argument rather than cite one. Control goal: should be solvable.

goal: The sum of the square root of 2 and the square root of 3 is irrational
note: Irrationality is not closed under addition, so no lemma covers this directly. Needs squaring to 5 + 2*sqrt(6) and citing irrationality of sqrt(6): at least two linked Mathlib results, neither of which mentions the goal.

goal: The determinant of the 3x3 matrix with rows (1,2,3), (4,5,6), (7,8,9) is zero
note: Only Matrix.det_fin_three (an expansion, not an answer) is relevant via Loogle. Expected failure mode is notation/plumbing (!![...] entries), not mathematics -- a bridge probe, not strong evidence about reasoning either way.

goal: Every non-constant polynomial with complex coefficients has a root in the complex numbers.
note: Complex.exists_root {f : ℂ[X]} (hf : 0 < degree f) : ∃ z, IsRoot f z, confirmed in Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Polynomial/Basic.lean, whose own docstring says it proves this using Liouville's theorem. No purely algebraic or real-analytic proof exists -- every known route needs complex analysis, a topological winding-number argument, or Galois theory. See docs/deep-tier-candidates.md.

goal: A function from the complex numbers to the complex numbers that is complex differentiable everywhere and whose values are bounded must be constant.
note: Differentiable.exists_eq_const_of_bounded {f : E → F} (hf : Differentiable ℂ f) (hb : IsBounded (Set.range f)) : ∃ c, f = Function.const E c, confirmed in Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Liouville.lean. Inherently complex-analytic -- bounds all derivatives from one bound on f via Cauchy's integral formula -- and the real-variable analogue is FALSE (sin x is real differentiable everywhere and bounded, not constant), so no elementary substitute can exist. See docs/deep-tier-candidates.md.

goal: Every subgroup of a free group is itself a free group.
note: subgroupIsFreeOfIsFree {G} [Group G] [IsFreeGroup G] (H : Subgroup G) : IsFreeGroup H, confirmed in Mathlib/GroupTheory/FreeGroup/NielsenSchreier.lean, docstring "The Nielsen-Schreier theorem". Classical proofs need covering-space topology or the combinatorial Reidemeister-Schreier method; no proof from the group axioms alone is known. Honest caveat: this is an `instance`, not a plain theorem, sitting on unfamiliar IsFreeGroupoid/Groupoid infrastructure -- expect this to test Lean-idiom translation as much as recognition. See docs/deep-tier-candidates.md.

goal: If p is a prime number and p to the power n divides the order of a finite group G, then G has a subgroup of order p to the power n.
note: Sylow.exists_subgroup_card_pow_prime [Finite G] (p : ℕ) {n} [Fact p.Prime] (hdvd : p^n ∣ Nat.card G) : ∃ K, Nat.card K = p^n, confirmed in Mathlib/GroupTheory/Sylow.lean. Borderline pick, flagged deliberately: needs a genuine group-action/orbit-counting idea, not reducible to induction on order alone, but the idea is textbook-clever rather than machinery from an outside field -- cut first if the tier needs trimming toward stricter cases. See docs/deep-tier-candidates.md.

goal: If a and n are coprime natural numbers, there are infinitely many prime numbers congruent to a modulo n.
note: Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_modEq (m : ℕ) {q a} (hq : q ≠ 0) (h : a.Coprime q) : ∃ p > m, p.Prime ∧ p ≡ a [MOD q], confirmed in Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean, docstring "Dirichlet's Theorem". The general theorem's only known proofs use Dirichlet L-functions (L(1,χ) ≠ 0 for every nontrivial character); no elementary proof of the general coprime case exists. Deepest citation target in the set -- buried behind hundreds of lines of L-function machinery, itself a real test of retrieval. See docs/deep-tier-candidates.md.
